fighting tax fraud and evasion, sharply cutting current spending, halving the president's salary, and subjecting FOBAPROA to a truth-commission review.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Andrés Manuel López Obrador","action":"set anti-corruption and austerity demands in the campaign platform","mechanism":"fiscal cuts, tax-compliance enforcement, and a truth commission for bank-rescue controversies","outcome":"intended a lower-spending, more accountability-focused fiscal program","dates":["2006"],"quantities":["half the president's salary"],"excerpt":"A la vez, urgía combatir el fraude y la evasión fiscal, así como recortar drásticamente los gastos corrientes, siendo el primer paso la reducción a la mitad del sueldo del presidente de la República. En cuanto a las actividades del FOBAPROA, serían investigadas por una Comisión de la Verdad.","locator":"extracted HTML block 30","attribution":"CIDOB political biography","period_fit":"2006 campaign platform","source_limitations":["Campaign platform text, not downstream spending or audit evidence.","Truth-commission language indicates intent, not completed investigation."],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"IMF-010","claim":"In 2022, retail fuel price stabilization reduced inflation by an estimated 2 percentage points, cost about 1.5% of GDP, and disproportionately benefited higher-income households.","claim_type":"interpretation","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"used fuel-price stabilization to cushion inflation","mechanism":"fuel subsidies and price smoothing","outcome":"lowered measured inflation while imposing a sizable budget cost and skewing benefits upward in the income distribution","dates":["2022"],"quantities":["2 percentage points","1.5 percent of GDP"],"excerpt":"• Retail fuel price stabilization has directly reduced cost pressures, lowering inflation by an estimated 2 percentage points this year. The measure has come at a sizeable budgetary cost, estimated at around 1.5 percent of GDP, and has disproportionately benefited higher income households. Furthermore, by diluting price signals, the policy has short-circuited the desirable adjustment in fuel demand.","locator":"page 19","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2022 inflation shock response","source_limitations":["IMF staff estimate, not an administrative microdata audit.","Distributional incidence is described qualitatively and may be model-based."],"question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"IMF-010","claim":"The 2022 household-inflation package relied on fuel subsidies and preexisting food-support measures, including retailer price restraints on 24 staple foods.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"launched anti-inflation household measures","mechanism":"fuel subsidies plus preexisting agricultural support and retailer price agreements","outcome":"supported household budgets and restrained some food-price increases at fiscal cost","dates":["2022"],"quantities":["MEX$395.4 billion","1.4 percent of GDP","24 core food items"],"excerpt":"Fuel subsidies lie at the heart of PACIC and are expected to cost the Federal government around MEX$395.4 billion (1.4 percent of GDP) by the end the year. Meanwhile, efforts to contain rising food costs have largely sought to leverage pre-existing agricultural support programs but also include an agreement with major retailers to limit prices increases for 24 core food items at no cost to the Federal government.","locator":"page 74","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2022 household inflation-response package","source_limitations":["IMF staff summary of the authorities' 2022 package; not all measures are quantified here.","Policy effects and implementation details are partly descriptive."],"question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"IMF-010","claim":"The 2023 draft budget increased spending by 8.5% nominally to fund social pensions, priority infrastructure, and agricultural supports, while leaving the tax code unchanged and keeping anti-evasion efforts.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"drafted the 2023 budget","mechanism":"higher expenditure on social programs, infrastructure, and targeted rural supports with unchanged tax code","outcome":"more spending on consumption support and investment while trying to preserve neutral fiscal stance","dates":["October 18, 2022","2023"],"quantities":["8.5 percent","0.1 percentage points of authorities’ projected GDP"],"excerpt":"Compared to the authorities estimated 2022 outturn, expenditure in 2023 is increased by 8.5 percent in nominal terms (or by 0.1 percentage points of authorities’ projected GDP). This increase accommodates higher spending of interest payments, some social programs—particularly (non-contributory) social pensions for the elderly—and priority infrastructure projects. In addition, the allotted funding for social programs related to fertilizers, procurement of national milk, and rural supplies has also been increased, though the size of the programs remains modest. On the revenue side, the budget entails no change in the tax code but highlights continued efforts to reduce tax evasion and avoidance.","locator":"page 13","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"late-2022 2023 budget drafting","source_limitations":["Staff report summarizes the 2023 draft budget rather than year-end outturn.","This is a proposed budget, not realized execution."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"IMF-010","claim":"In April 2021, Mexico enacted a law restricting workforce subcontracting to curb labor-law violations and tax evasion, and made non-compliance a criminal offense.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"enacted subcontracting restrictions","mechanism":"banning third-party management of workers and tightening registration and reporting requirements","outcome":"curbed outsourcing abuse and turned non-compliance into a criminal offense","dates":["April 2021"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"In April 2021, the authorities enacted new legislation restricting the subcontracting of the workforce, with the aim of preventing the violation of labor law and tax evasion. The new law bans service firms from providing employees to be supervised and managed by a third-party, while it still allows subcontracting of services if the employees are monitored by the firm providing the service.1 The legislation also tightened registration and reporting requirements. Non-compliance with this new subcontracting law became a criminal offence.","locator":"page 69","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"April 2021 labor-law reform with 2021-2022 implementation effects","source_limitations":["Describes the law's enactment and intended purpose; implementation effects are inferred from later data.","Legal text does not by itself show enforcement quality."],"question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"IMF-010","claim":"Mexico approved a new electricity law that replaced auctions with nonmarket policies, shifted regulatory power to CFE, and disrupted contracts from the 2013 reform.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"changed electricity-market rules","mechanism":"moving from auctions to nonmarket-based policies and empowering the state-owned utility CFE","outcome":"created conflicts of interest and disrupted existing contracts","dates":["2022","2013"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"A new electricity law, however, was approved and has replaced auctions by nonmarket-based policies, with regulatory power given to the Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE), the state-owned electricity company. This has created conflicts of interest and disrupted contracts signed under the 2013 reform.","locator":"page 33","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2022 energy-policy change under the 4T","source_limitations":["IMF staff characterization of the energy-law shift; it does not independently adjudicate legality.","The passage is an assessment of policy effects in 2022."],"question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"LAW-005","claim":"The 8 December 2022 fuel-stimulus notice set reduced excise support for gasoline and diesel for 10-16 December 2022, with gasoline under 91 octanes and diesel receiving nonzero subsidies and premium gasoline receiving none.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"Mexican fiscal authorities","action":"published a fuel-stimulus schedule","mechanism":"setting lower excise rates and per-liter stimulus amounts for selected fuels","outcome":"temporarily reduced fuel taxes for the specified week","dates":["December 8, 2022","December 10-16, 2022"],"quantities":["26.96%","59.77%","$1.4803","$3.6071","$4.0114","$4.6375"],"excerpt":"Artículo Primero. Los porcentajes del estímulo fiscal para el periodo comprendido del 10 al 16 de diciembre de 2022, aplicables a los combustibles automotrices son los siguientes: Combustible Porcentaje de Estímulo Gasolina menor a 91 octanos 26.96% Gasolina mayor o igual a 91 octanos y combustibles no fósiles 0.00% Diésel 59.77% Artículo Segundo. Los montos del estímulo fiscal para el periodo comprendido del 10 al 16 de diciembre de 2022, aplicables a los combustibles automotrices son los siguientes: Combustible Monto del estímulo fiscal (pesos/litro) Gasolina menor a 91 octanos $1.4803 Gasolina mayor o igual a 91 octanos y combustibles no fósiles $0.0000 Diésel $3.6071","locator":"extracted HTML block 2","attribution":"Acuerdo 173/2022, Diario Oficial de la Federación","period_fit":"December 10-16, 2022 fuel-stimulus schedule","source_limitations":["Official notice gives rates and effective period but not downstream pass-through or household incidence.","It is a legal schedule, not a performance evaluation."],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"source_id":"IMF-010","claim":"Mexico had timely, comprehensive economic data judged adequate for surveillance and subscribed to the IMF SDDS.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"maintained macroeconomic data reporting standards","mechanism":"timely publication of comprehensive official statistics under SDDS and Article VIII obligations","outcome":"surveillance data were considered adequate by the IMF","dates":["2022"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Mexico has accepted the obligations of Article VIII, sections 2, 3, and 4. Comprehensive economic data are available for Mexico on a timely basis and economic data are adequate for surveillance. It subscribes to the SDDS.","locator":"page 98","attribution":"IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (2022 Article IV Consultation)","period_fit":"2022 IMF surveillance and data-quality assessment","source_limitations":["Institutional IMF data-quality assessment, not evidence of AMLO's personal choices.","Country-level assessment only."],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false}],"rejected_or_omitted_passages":["Omitted long biographical passages on family background, early career, and electoral history that did not add new 5B evidence beyond the platform and governing episodes captured above.","Omitted repeated IMF tables and charts that restated the same macroeconomic and fiscal facts already captured in narrative passages."],"unresolved_gaps":["No direct packet evidence on how economic officials were appointed, retained, or replaced on the basis of performance versus loyalty (5B.2).","The packet contains mostly campaign statements, IMF staff assessments, and legal notices rather than independent audit-level verification of every implementation effect."]}
